items.title: General strike called for November 11
items.body: CC.OO. and UGT have called a 24-hour general strike for Wednesday, November 11, after a tenants' movement demanded action on housing. Large factories and supply chains could face disruption. Four other representative unions have refused to join, calling the strike political.

items.title: Madrid–Andalusia rail closure raises travel costs
items.body: High-speed rail between Madrid and Andalusia remains closed after the Urda crash killed 69 people. About 28,500 rail trips are unavailable daily. Alternatives cost more: a Madrid–Sevilla bus ticket costs €85, and an Air Europa flight averages €125.

items.title: Inflation and mortgage costs await next government
items.body: Spain's next government will inherit CPI inflation of 4.9% and an October Euribor of 3.2%, keeping pressure on household budgets and mortgages. Conflict and shipping threats are keeping energy prices high. Employment has reached a record 22.8 million, but experts expect growth to slow.

items.title: Feijóo pledges housing decree repeal before election
items.body: PP candidate Alberto Núñez Feijóo pledged to repeal the housing decrees and said a Vox coalition "doesn't depend on me". The decrees remain in force pending parliamentary confirmation. Housing, rail safety, and corruption dominated party messages ahead of the November 29 election.

items.title: El Hierro declares social emergency over arrivals
items.body: El Hierro's island council has declared a social emergency as migrant arrivals strain reception services. About 4,000 people have reached the Canaries by sea so far in November. The council wants more staff and faster transfers; the central government has called a meeting for November 10.

items.title: Catalan police arrest 50 over fake contracts
items.body: Catalan police arrested 50 people, including 43 business owners, over an alleged fake-job-contract network. Investigators say it charged migrants up to €30,000 to help secure entry or legal residence in Spain. The case highlights fraud risks around work-based residency applications.

items.title: November 7 resolution boosts heat pump incentives
items.body: A resolution published on November 7 boosts energy-saving certificate incentives for replacing boilers with heat pumps. Multipliers are x2 for houses, x2.5 for individual flat systems, x3 for central systems, and x4 for switching individual systems to central heating. Vulnerable households can get a further 50%.

items.title: Barcelona tenants win rulings against tourist licences
items.body: Two Catalan high court rulings back Barcelona's withdrawal of tourist-flat licences at a 120-home rental building. The court found that homes with active rental contracts were not immediately available to tourists, as the law requires. The rulings could protect other tenants, but a Supreme Court appeal remains possible.

items.title: Public healthcare satisfaction falls as waits persist
items.body: Satisfaction with Spain's public health system has fallen to 6.19 out of 10, half a point below 2018. In December, 4,072,139 people awaited a specialist appointment, with average waits exceeding 102 days. Primary care receives only 13-14% of public health spending, against the 25% its professionals seek.

items.title: Murcia fashion student wins World Skills bronze
items.body: Vocational student Juan García Ortiz, 20, won fashion bronze at World Skills in Shanghai with 729 points, Spain's only medal at this edition. His former school in Lorca now has a waiting list. Murcia has expanded vocational places by 45% and leads Spain in job placement for intermediate-level vocational training.

items.title: Flat buyers answer for past community fee debts
items.body: Under existing law, a purchased flat guarantees unpaid community fees for the current year and three previous calendar years. Buyers should obtain the community's debt certificate before signing. Special levies fall to whoever owns the property when payment is due, so checking meeting minutes also matters.

items.title: Bus company faces sanction case over booking fees
items.body: The Consumer Affairs Ministry has opened sanction proceedings against a bus company over alleged hidden booking fees and unfair refund terms. It says management fees appear only at the final booking stage. A fine could reach up to €1 million or six to eight times the illicit profit.
